why: Grabbing the g5 pawn with a once-defended square ignored the gxh4 threat and cost the knight.
The e4 knight could be won with Ne7 and the queen lift, but Bd7 missed it and allowed Ne5.
The queen was chased by the bishop and moved again to a square that blocks the c8 bishop, instead of retreating to d8 and developing.
Bxh5 and Bxc5 were threatened, and Nxe4 won a pawn, but Nf6 left the c5 knight to be deflected.
In a pawn race g4 creates the fastest passed pawn, while Kf2 let Black push the b-pawn.
The e4 pawn was loose and Qxe4 simply won it, but Bg3 let Black keep it.
Recapturing with the f-pawn weakened the king shelter, while Bxe5 recaptured with a piece.
Castling queenside was the useful move, while Bc5 left the king in the centre and the bishop was traded off.
Trading the h6 bishop for the g7 bishop was right, and Qg5 left it hanging to Bxh6.
The king on f2 faces checks and the e6 pawn was loose, but Rg5 ignored both.
The check Rae1+ ignored Black's threat and Bg6+ would have won the g3 pawn.
Be7 took away the e6 defender of d5 so the pawn fell.
The knight on g4 was chased by h3 and ended on the rim, while Nd5 centralised it.
d6 allowed Nb6 forking a8 and c8, which also won the loose f6 pawn.
